risks.title: The CIS CI/CD role trusts every repo in the org, so a new AA-Booking repo would inherit near-admin AWS rights
risks.evidence: `accounts/aa365/cicd.tf:34` trust sub = `repo:AdventureAsia365-Ecosys*/*:*` (any repo, any ref). The same role has AmazonRDSFullAccess, SecretsManagerReadWrite, ECS/S3/VPC/Lambda full access (`cicd.tf:42-53`) and iam:CreateRole/PutRolePolicy/PassRole/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on Resource "*" (`cicd.tf:147-163`). Role ARNs are not secret. Any workflow in a new repo (AA-Booking) or on any branch can assume it, a privilege-escalation path. The TripPlanner deploy role already shows the scoped pattern (`tripplanner.tf:482-548`).
risks.recommendation: Ship this in the Lane C Infra PR, before `gh repo create AA-Booking`: narrow the `aa-cis-dev-role` sub to `AA-CIS-App*` and `AA-CIS-Infra*` only (a StringLike list), and give Booking its own `aa-booking-dev-app-deploy` role. That role gets only: ECR push on its own repo, ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition, UpdateService/DescribeServices on its own service, and iam:PassRole on its own exec and task roles only. Also add an `iam:TagRole` grant for `role/aa-booking-dev-*` on the CI role (`cicd.tf:320-325` pattern), or the apply fails. Never give the Booking repo the `prod` environment secrets used by db-migrate and terraform-apply (`db-migrate.yml:36`).

risks.title: Subagent guardrails only cover Bash; GitHub, Linear and Vercel MCP write tools are not blocked
risks.evidence: `.claude/settings.json` registers the PreToolUse hook with `"matcher": "Bash"` only. `.claude/hooks/subagent-guardrails.sh:12-19` matches shell strings only, so the GitHub MCP tools (merge_pull_request, create_repository, push_files, create_or_update_file, delete_repository), Linear save_issue/save_comment and Vercel create_project are not covered. Gaps inside Bash too: `gh api ... -f k=v` POSTs without `-X`, `aws ecs execute-command`, `aws iam *`, `aws lambda invoke` and `aws s3 cp` writes are not in the pattern list. The pilot plan (`11-next-session-team-pilot.md:10-12`) assumes subagents cannot merge or create repos.
risks.recommendation: Before Gate 1, widen the matcher to `Bash|mcp__plugin_github_github__.*|mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_.*|mcp__claude_ai_Vercel__.*`, or add a second hook that denies MCP write tools when `agent_id` is present. Add `gh api .* -f`, `aws ecs execute-command`, `aws iam` and `aws lambda (invoke|update)` to the patterns. Until then, every lane brief must also say: do not use MCP write tools.

risks.title: Booking jobs in `shared.job` would freeze the CIS deploy train
risks.evidence: The CIS deploy guard blocks while any `shared.job` row is queued or running, with no kind or app filter (`apps/AA-CIS-App/.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml:29-33`). The worker claim is kind-filtered (`shared/jobs/queue.py:96`), so a CIS worker would not run Booking jobs, but those jobs still count in the gate. AA-678 says "reuse the job-runner pattern (catalog sync, inquiry intake, notifications)". ADR 0003 decision 4 (`docs/adr/0003-one-durable-job-model.md:204-208`) leaves a second repo enqueuing into `shared.job` deferred (AA-751). The AA-678 comment also asks Booking to copy the AA-725 guard, which would need the CIS ADMIN_SECRET.
risks.recommendation: Decide in the Booking ADR. Either Booking keeps its own `booking.job` table and worker (library code copied or vendored from `shared/jobs/`), or the CIS deploy-gate is changed to count only CIS kinds first. Booking must never hold the CIS ADMIN_SECRET. It needs its own deploy gate on its own job table. Not needed for the S235 bootstrap (health only), but `bk-001` should not assume either way.

risks.title: DB role `booking` has no defined home, and the grant migrations can silently no-op for good
risks.evidence: `schema-ownership.md:31-34` (rule 3) says Infra owns the DB roles but keeps no schema SQL. DB Migrate only accepts the owners cis, tripplanner and booking (`db-migrate.yml:52`) and runs as the CIS task's DATABASE_URL (`db/run_migration.py:33`). Per tfvars this is master user `aa_cis_admin` (`accounts/aa365/terraform.tfvars:21`), so every `booking.*` object will be owned by aa_cis_admin, not by `booking`. The 007b precedent committed a plaintext role password to git, and it had to be rotated (`apps/AA-CIS-App/api/migrations/007b_create_app_user.sql:10-16,25-27`). The cross-app grants are guarded by `IF EXISTS (pg_roles ...)` and register their version anyway (`apps/AA-TripPlanner-Web/migrations/008_inquiry_outbox.sql:43-50,56-58`). A CIS or TripPlanner grant migration applied before the role exists becomes a permanent, registered no-op.
risks.recommendation: `bk-001` does: `CREATE ROLE booking LOGIN` with no PASSWORD clause (guarded), `CREATE SCHEMA booking`, grants of USAGE and DML to booking, and `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE aa_cis_admin IN SCHEMA booking ... TO booking`. Nghiệp then sets the password out-of-band with ALTER ROLE plus the `aa-booking/dev/database-url` secret, because secrets writes are blocked for agents. Write grant migrations without the `IF EXISTS` guard, so they fail loudly instead of registering a no-op. Fixed order, run one at a time: Infra apply → bk-001 → password → CIS grant migration (SELECT on `shared.destinations` and the photo views, INSERT on `shared.llm_call_log`) → tp-009 (SELECT on `tripplanner.v_inquiry_outbox`). Record the rule-3 clarification (role SQL lives in the owner's bk-001) in `schema-ownership.md` (orchestrator).

risks.title: API routing: the existing REST API → NLB → ALB path cannot route Booking by host, and changing the CIS API Gateway module would redeploy CIS
risks.evidence: ALB is one target group (port 8000, `/health`) with default-forward listeners on 80 and 443 (`modules/alb/main.tf:45-97`). API Gateway reaches it through the VPC-link NLB to ALB:80 with `uri = http://<nlb_dns>/...` (`modules/api_gateway/main.tf:36,336`), so the original Host header is lost. A host-based ALB rule cannot see `api-booking.*`. Every route is hand-listed, and the deployment hash forces a CIS stage redeploy on any integration change (`modules/api_gateway/main.tf:356-370`). The custom domain and ACM cert are CIS-only (`terraform.tfvars:25-26`).
risks.recommendation: In `booking.tf`: create a new ALB target group `aa-booking-dev-api-tg` (port 8000, `/health`) with an ALB listener rule on a path prefix (for example `/booking/*`) or on a custom header. Better: a separate API Gateway HTTP API v2 with a VPC Link v2 to the ALB listener, and its own custom domain. This leaves `modules/api_gateway` untouched. The custom domain needs an ACM cert and Namecheap DNS, which only Nghiệp can do.

risks.title: The ECS module cannot be reused for Booking, and a new service has no image to start
risks.evidence: `modules/ecs/main.tf` bundles the cluster, CIS ECR `aws_ecr_repository.api` (:227), the CIS task definitions with CIS secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, `ADMIN_SECRET`, `JWT_SECRET`, `OPENAI` at :285-296) and the CIS service (:328). The Booking ADR should state that Booking reads only views (no `published_tours` grant) and that AA-679 waits for the CIS catalog views, CIS outbox and `catalog.tour.v1.json`. Track the ISO-country mapping (`shared.countries`, CIS-owned) as a CIS dependency.

risks.title: Migration-number and Infra-repo collisions between Lane A and Lane C

result.summary: Lens: CIS portal and admin API for lane B (AA-797, AA-796, AA-798), checked against lane A. I read code at AA-CIS-App main 20a2387, CONTEXT.md, report 12 §2.3/§3, plan 11, the Linear issues and their comments, and db-schema-reference.md (verified S234, migration 222). Everything was read-only. Plan 11 assumes that lane B is "frontend-only PRs merge any time" (11-next-session-team-pilot.md:34). That is not true. All three lane-B issues change the backend, and AA-798 needs a migration. AA-796 as scoped edits services/jobs/t2_rewrite_job.py:224-235, which is the T2 job that lane A is rewriting and rerunning in this session. The biggest architectural finding is schema drift. The live shared.v_tenant_monthly_usage shape (billing_month, llm_cost_usd, quota_*_pct), shared.membership_plans and shared.tenants.plan_id are not created by any repo migration. The only definition of the view is 007_tenant_usage.sql:12-22, which has a different column set (month, total_calls, ...). That is exactly why GET /tenants/{id}/usage returns 500 (admin.py:359-368). AA-798's view migration will collide with the 007 shape in the CI integration DB. Other findings with real risk: (1) the tenant-facing GET /v1/billing returns llm_cost_usd from the same view (v1_tours.py:282), so once AA-798 makes it real, tenants would see AA's actual LLM spend; (2) once AA-797 makes suspend/offboard work, any staff role (reviewer and content, not just admin) can call PATCH/DELETE/offboard/generate-key on tenants through the BFF (rbac.ts:66,75-78); (3) the list endpoint hides inactive tenants (admin.py:296), so a working Suspend toggle makes the tenant disappear with no way to resume it from the UI; (4) AA-796's scope misses tenant endpoints that still expose scores: /v1/tours/{id} returns pt.* (v1_tours.py:712-733) and /v1/tours/{id}/full returns full quality_scores, generated_content and raw_tours rows (v1_tours.py:665-707); (5) get_tenant_details (admin.py:550+) also drives the Master Content page (master-content/page.tsx:850), so lane B edits there can break a lane-unrelated admin page. My recommendation: lane B is ONE serial agent (797, then 798, then 796), with AA-796 done at the tenant-API projection layer, not in t2_rewrite_job.py. Lane B backend PRs join lane A's serial backend train and never deploy while the T2 rerun or the r5 checkpoint jobs are queued or running. The orchestrator owns rbac.ts, CONTEXT.md, the schema reference, migration number 223 and the AA-CIS-Infra migration copy.

risks.title: Schema drift: the live usage view, membership_plans and tenants.plan_id are not in any repo migration
risks.evidence: The only definition of shared.v_tenant_monthly_usage in either repo is api/migrations/007_tenant_usage.sql:12-22 (columns: tenant_id, month, total_calls, successful_calls, rate_limited_calls, avg_response_ms, endpoints_used). The live view has billing_month, tours_quota_monthly, quota_tours_pct, llm_cost_usd and more (db-schema-reference.md:1288-1306). Grepping quota_tours_pct/billing_month finds them only in routers, never in migrations (AA-CIS-App and infra/AA-CIS-Infra). shared.membership_plans (db-schema-reference.md:928-939) and shared.tenants.plan_id (:1228, FK :1735) have no DDL in api/migrations either; 042_tenants_gdpr_quota.sql adds only cancelled_at/cancellation_reason. The 500 on GET /tenants/{id}/usage is this drift: admin.py:359-368 selects month/total_calls/... from the live view, which no longer has them. Integration tests build the DB from repo migrations (tests/integration/conftest.py:60-114), so CI sees the 007 shape, not the live one.
risks.recommendation: Before writing AA-798's migration, dump pg_get_viewdef('shared.v_tenant_monthly_usage') and the DDL of membership_plans and the plan_id column from Dev (read-only SELECT via ECS exec). Make migration 223 a baseline: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS membership_plans, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS plan_id, then DROP VIEW IF EXISTS plus CREATE VIEW, with explicit re-GRANTs. CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW will fail on the 007-shaped CI database because it cannot rename or drop columns. First check pg_depend for views that depend on it, so no CASCADE surprise hits Dev. Ship it through the DB Migrate workflow, in the same batched Infra approval as lane C.

Remove the twin fabricated defaults in v1_tours.py:352-361 ($299, 50 tours, starter) together with admin_pipeline.py:4983-4992. AA-798's scope names only the admin copy.

result.summary: Architect review (lens: AA-CIS-App backend, read-only) of what S235 Lane A will touch. Repo checked at main 20a2387, clean, with one registered worktree. Bottom line: Lane A is really two tracks whose files barely overlap. Track A-T2 (AA-792, AA-794) lives in services/content_generation/* and the T2 job. Track A-T9 (AA-785, AA-786, AA-776, AA-773, AA-774, AA-775) lives in services/acp_content_writing/* and services/acp_shared/{atom_seed,place_cards,brand_pack}.py. The two tracks can be built in parallel. Inside A-T9, every issue pairs up with another on the same hot file, so that track must be strictly serial. Five cross-cutting hazards decide the plan. (1) The writer prompt builder is shared by A1, T2 and the Bedrock Batch path, and nothing pins the A1 prompt bytes. (2) The F1 number matcher is a shared utility used by A1 grounding, the T3 check on T2 output, source facts and T10. (3) The seed's line format is parsed in at least 5 places with no single definition. (4) Deploy Dev also fires on frontend/** pushes and is guarded by shared.job, so Lane B is neither 'frontend-only' nor 'merge any time'. (5) The T2 brand path has two different 'has brand' tests, its own copy of the brand-rules query, and an Adventure Asia (AA) brand-identity fallback that conflicts with the tenant-voice goal of AA-792. The T2 rerun as scoped (verify AA-792/793/794) also mixes a writer change with a judge-rubric change. It also depends on AA-793, which is not scheduled, and on a rerun method nobody has defined. The orchestrator should settle these before Gate 1.

The itinerary JSON spec in the user prompt also demands NEUTRAL voice (prompts.py:374-383). Tests only check that sync and batch match and that 'neutral' appears (tests/unit/test_aa724_writer_neutral_voice.py:25-66; test_aa606_bedrock_batch.py:124). No SHA pins the A1 system/user prompt, whereas the T9 prompt is pinned (test_aa771_s234_voice_contract.py:450-452).

risks.title: The T2 brand path has two different 'has brand' tests, its own brand-rules query, and an Adventure Asia fallback
risks.evidence: T2 loads brand rules with its own SELECT using ORDER BY version DESC and no brand_name/brand_type/default_cta (services/jobs/t2_rewrite_job.py:81-87). brand_pack orders by (brand_name='default') DESC, version DESC (services/acp_shared/brand_pack.py:43), so T2 can pick a different row from the one T8/T9/T10 use. The judge runs only if has_brand_signals (core_idea, mindset or voice; brand_fit.py:79-91), while brand_pack.has_brand uses core_idea, style_guide or system_prompt (brand_pack.py:102). Without judge_brand_fit, i.e. the judge was skipped or failed (judge_node.py:124-127, 184-187), brand_audit_node reviews tenant copy 'against Adventure Asia brand standards' (brand_audit_node.py:271-278, brand_standards.py:3-18). That rubric REQUIRES 'Curated/Refined/Tailored', which the core forbidden list bans. The writer also always gets the AA core forbidden list on top of the tenant's own (batch_prompt.py:111-125, forbidden_words.py:19-22).
risks.recommendation: Make AA-792 load T2 brand data through brand_pack.fetch_brand_pack_conn and render it (or a T2 variant of render_brand_block), so T2, T8, T9 and T10 read the same row. For is_tenant_rewrite, replace the AA-identity audit fallback with the compiled tenant rubric (brand_pack.compile_rubric) or skip it. Pick one 'has brand' test. Ask Nghiệp whether the AA core forbidden list still binds tenant voice.

# ADR 0004 — AA-Booking: stack, repo layout, runtime and bootstrap on acc2

- **Status:** Proposed (14/10/2026, S235 Gate 0.5 — architect draft). Accepted once Nghiệp signs off decisions 1–9 and the open decisions in the last section.
- **Scope:** AA-Ecosys (new repo AA-Booking, AA-CIS-Infra, AA-CIS-App and AA-TripPlanner-Web for the read grants).
- **Implements:** ADR 0001 decisions 5–7 (placement, contracts, one IaC repo), ADR 0002 (only CIS writes content), ADR 0003 (one durable job model). Closes ecosystem review §11 open question 5 ("Does AAA follow the CIS stack?").
- **Related:** AA-677 (ERD v2, done), AA-678 (bootstrap), AA-679 (catalog sync), AA-680 (identity), AA-681 (trip case), AA-682 (operations), AA-683 (UI spec), AA-751 (second repo on `shared.job`).

## Context

AA-Booking (AAA) is built in-house from scratch (Nghiệp, 28/09 and S226). The inputs are the Quanskill PRD (09/06/2026), the v1 ERD, the handover review (10/06/2026), about 110 Figma screens and ERD v2 (`docs/AAA/erd-v2/`). No vendor code was delivered. ADR 0001 fixes where Booking runs: acc2, the shared RDS, schema `booking`, provisioned by AA-CIS-Infra, with no new accounts. It does not fix how Booking is built.

What already exists:
- **DB Migrate** accepts `booking/NNN_*.sql` and registers `bk-NNN` (`AA-CIS-Infra/.github/workflows/db-migrate.yml`).
- TripPlanner writes `inquiry.submitted` v1 into `tripplanner.outbox` and exposes `tripplanner.v_inquiry_outbox` (tp-008).
- CIS runs FastAPI + asyncpg on ECS behind API Gateway (REST) → VPC link → NLB → ALB, deploys through GitHub OIDC, and enforces "done" as merge + CI + rollout COMPLETED + live verify.

What it costs to differ from CIS: a second CI, deploy, auth and testing toolchain for a solo-run program.

## Decisions

1. **Stack = the CIS stack.**
   - Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, asyncpg with plain SQL repositories (no ORM in request paths).
   - Frontend: Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript with `@tanstack/react-query` and `@tanstack/react-table`.
   - Database: PostgreSQL 15 on the shared RDS.
   - The frontend copies the CIS UI kit (`app/_kit`) and brand tokens until the shared design-system package (ADR 0001 decision 7, AA-655) is published, then switches to it.

2. **Repo `AdventureAsia365-Ecosys/AA-Booking`, layout:**
   ```
   backend/        FastAPI app (app/main.py, app/routers/, app/db.py, app/settings.py), tests/unit, tests/integration, Dockerfile
   migrations/     NNN_<name>.sql — owner key bk-NNN
   frontend/       Next.js — staff admin first; customer surface after the scope decision (open decision 4)
   docs/adr/       repo ADRs; 0001 cites this ADR
   docs/erd/       ERD v2 (moved from AA-Ecosys/docs/AAA/erd-v2)
   CONTEXT.md, README.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md   (English)
   ```
   - Trunk-based (ADR-2026-023): feature branch → PR → required CI → human merge to `main`.
   - Commits follow the program format (`feat|fix|chore|refactor|docs: …` + `Refs AA-xxx`).

3. **CI: five required checks**, mirroring CIS names so branch protection reads the same:
   - **Lint** (ruff).
   - **Security Audit** (pip-audit, failing, unlike CIS's report-only).
   - **Unit Tests**, including a migration guard: each `migrations/*.sql` is wrapped in `BEGIN; … COMMIT;`, registers its own `bk-NNN` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, and creates or alters nothing outside schema `booking`.
   - **Integration Tests**: Postgres 15 service with a stub `shared` schema; apply all migrations in order, then call `/booking/health/ready`.
   - **Docker Build Check**, with a Trivy report and an SBOM.
   - Non-required: **Frontend Build** (`next build` + eslint). Later: UI smoke on Vercel preview (AA-732 pattern).

4. **Deploy path.**
   - `deploy-dev.yml` on push to `main`.
   - GitHub OIDC → role `aa-booking-dev-app-deploy`. This role is new and least-privilege: ECR push to `aa-booking-dev-api` only, `ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition`/`DescribeTaskDefinition`, `UpdateService`/`DescribeServices` on Booking services only, and `iam:PassRole` on the two Booking roles only. AA-Booking never receives the broad `aa-cis-dev-role` ARN.
   - Image tag = git SHA (immutable).

   - Once Booking owns job kinds, add a pre-deploy guard on its own kinds (AA-725 pattern).
   - Frontend: Vercel Git integration.
   - "Done" follows `aa-ship`: merge + CI + rollout COMPLETED + live verify.

5. **Runtime, provisioned by AA-CIS-Infra** in a self-contained `accounts/aa365/booking.tf` (the `tripplanner.tf` pattern; no existing CIS resource modified except one new alb module output):
   - ECR `aa-booking-dev-api` (scan on push, keep last 10).
   - Log group `/ecs/aa-booking-dev`.
   - Own execution role (GetSecretValue on `booking/dev/*` only) and own task role. No Bedrock and no CIS secrets; add only when a feature needs them.
   - Secret `booking/dev/database-url`: a placeholder in Terraform with `ignore_changes`; the value is set out-of-band.
   - ECS service `aa-booking-dev-api` on the existing `aa-cis-dev-cluster`:
     - 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GB, FARGATE base 1 + FARGATE_SPOT;
     - circuit breaker with rollback;
     - `ignore_changes = [task_definition, desired_count]`;
     - `enable_execute_command`;
     - existing private subnets and app security group.
   - Routing:
     - ALB target group (port 8000, health check `/booking/health`);
     - listener rule `path-pattern /booking/*` on the ALB **HTTP** listener (the NLB → ALB hop is port 80), which needs a new `http_listener_arn` output in `modules/alb`;
     - a separate REST API `aa-booking-dev` reusing the existing VPC link: `ANY /booking/{proxy+}` → `http://<nlb>/booking/{proxy}`;
     - custom domain `api-booking.lumiguides.it.com` if the ACM certificate covers it; otherwise the execute-api URL for Dev until a certificate is issued.
   - A worker service is added only with the first job kind (decision 8).
   - Rough cost: one 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GB Fargate task, mostly on Spot, is a few USD per month. No new ALB, NLB or NAT.
   - IAM bootstrap order: first add a `BookingRoleTagging` statement (`iam:TagRole`/`UntagRole` on `role/aa-booking-dev-*`) to `aa-cis-dev-role` and apply it. Only then apply `booking.tf` (same propagation trap as `TripPlannerRoleTagging`).

6. **Database role and grants (ADR 0002 decision 4 in the database).**
   - Login role `booking`: rights only on schema `booking`.
   - Reads outside its schema are granted only by the owner, in the owner's migration, guarded `IF EXISTS (role booking)`:
     - CIS migration (next number, e.g. 223): `USAGE` on `shared` + `SELECT` on `shared.v_tour_photos`, `shared.v_destination_photos` and `shared.destinations` (a view `shared.v_destinations` is preferred if CIS adds one), plus the catalog views when AA-679 defines them;
     - TripPlanner `tp-009`: `USAGE` on `tripplanner` + `SELECT` on `tripplanner.v_inquiry_outbox`.
   - Booking gets no `shared.job` grant before AA-751 and no `shared.llm_call_log` grant before it calls an LLM.
   - Role creation: `bk-001` creates `booking` **NOLOGIN** if it is missing, so the file is self-contained and idempotent. A one-off approved step then sets `LOGIN PASSWORD` from the value stored in `booking/dev/database-url`. No password is ever in Git.

7. **Migrations.**
   - Authored in `AA-Booking/migrations/NNN_*.sql`, key `bk-NNN`.
   - A byte-identical copy goes in `AA-CIS-Infra/db/migrations/booking/NNN_*.sql`.
   - Applied to Dev by **DB Migrate** (`check` → `apply`) from `main` of AA-CIS-Infra, before any app code that needs it merges.
   - `docs/architecture/db-schema-reference.md` is regenerated after each structural migration.
   - `bk-001` is a **first slice**, not the whole ERD v2:
     - schema, role, grants, default privileges;
     - enums `record_status`, `staff_role` (if open decision 1 keeps a Booking staff table), `trip_case_status`, `source_system`;
     - identity: `customers`, `customer_otps`, `customer_sessions`, and `staff_users` subject to open decision 1;
     - geography: `areas`, `country_profiles`, `media_files`;
     - intake core: `trip_cases` (without `trip_plan_id`), `trip_case_countries`, `trip_case_legs`, `trip_case_status_history`, a `trip_case_status_transitions` table + trigger that rejects illegal status jumps (AA-678 harness comment);
     - cross-cutting: `inbox_events` (unique on `(source, contract, idempotency_key)`), `audit_logs`.

     Catalog and inventory tables (`suppliers`, `hotels`, `activities`, `trip_plans*`, `destination_profiles`, `entity_media`) follow in `bk-002`, after the `catalog.tour.v1` contract and the country ISO decision. Versions, operations and money tables (`trip_case_versions*`, `trip_case_checks`, `staff_assignments`, `supplier_*`, `invoices`, `invoice_items`, `payment_schedule`, `payments`, `notifications`) follow in `bk-003` with AA-681/682. Reason: PostgreSQL enum values cannot be removed or renamed cheaply, and several FKs depend on undecided contracts.

8. **Deferred work uses the one job model (ADR 0003).**
   - `inbox_events` is the durable record of what was consumed.
   - Processing (inquiry intake, later catalog sync and notifications) runs as `shared.job` kinds in the Booking namespace once AA-751 grants Booking `INSERT`/`SELECT` on its own kinds. They run on a Booking-owned worker service (same image, `python -m worker`) that claims only Booking kinds.
   - The CIS Deploy Dev guard must then filter on CIS kinds, so Booking work does not block CIS deploys, and the reverse.
   - No in-process `asyncio.create_task` in request paths.

9. **Health and readiness are separate.**
   - `/booking/health` = process liveness, with no DB call. The ALB health check uses it, so a DB outage or a missing grant cannot trip the ECS circuit breaker into a rollback loop.
   - `/booking/health/ready` = DB connectivity + `bk-001` present in `shared.schema_versions`. Smoke tests and alarms use it.

## Open decisions (must be answered at Gate 1)

1. **Staff identity.**
   - (a) One store: Booking staff log in through the CIS staff login (`shared.admin_users`, AA-656). `booking.staff_users` becomes a thin profile keyed by `admin_users.id` (Booking role `admin|sales|content_creator`, no password).
   - (b) Booking keeps its own `staff_users` with its own auth.
   - Recommended: (a). It matches AA-680 "no separate staff user store". It needs a CIS migration adding email and the Booking roles, or a role-mapping table, and a token-verification contract.
   - Figma password-reset screens and the "Super Admin" label must then be mapped onto it.
2. **`bk-001` scope:** the first slice above, versus the whole ERD v2 as AA-678's Done-when literally says.
3. **Booking API hostname and certificate** (`api-booking.lumiguides.it.com` or execute-api for Dev).
4. **Customer surface:** does Booking build PRD §7.3 Discovery, or does TripPlanner stay the discovery/inquiry front, with Booking's customer app limited to sign-in, My Trips and My Payments?
5. **Guest inquiries** (`customer: null` in the contract): park in `inbox_events` until contact data exists, or allow nullable `trip_cases.customer_id`.
6. **Content boundary for AAA-authored activities and country text:** commercial data owned by Booking, or content that must be authored in CIS (ADR 0002 "Revisit").
7. **Job kind prefix** (`bk_*` vs AA-751's `aab_*`).

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - one toolchain;
  - CI, deploy and done-rules are copied, not invented;
  - least-privilege DB and IAM from the first commit;
  - schema ownership is enforced by the database and the migration guard;
  - Dev cost is marginal (one small Fargate task on an existing cluster, ALB and NLB).
- **Negative / cost:**
  - Booking shares the CIS ALB, NLB, VPC link and RDS, so an incident or maintenance on those affects both apps;
  - path-prefix routing ties Booking's public paths to `/booking/*`;
  - grants depend on CIS and TripPlanner migrations, so cross-repo ordering must be planned;
  - the UI kit is copied until AA-655 ships;
  - the `bk-001` first slice means later `ALTER`s on an empty schema.

## Alternatives considered

- **Laravel/PHP**: the handover's "Spatie" permission tables suggest Quanskill's stack. Rejected: no code was delivered, and it would mean a second CI/deploy/auth path.
- **Lambda + HTTP API** (TripPlanner pattern). Rejected for the main API: OTP sessions, staff CRUD and a long-running consumer fit a container service, and CIS's ECS deploy and DB Migrate tooling already target ECS. It can be revisited for a stateless public read API.
- **Own ALB/NLB or own cluster.** Rejected for Dev (cost, more Terraform). Revisit for staging/prod isolation.
- **Host header routing on the existing ALB.** Rejected: API Gateway integrations call the NLB by DNS name, so the client's Host header does not reach the ALB.
- **Whole ERD v2 in `bk-001`.** Rejected (see decision 7).
- **Separate database or account.** Rejected by ADR 0001.
